title: Reasons and Results at the Lake

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *porque* from A1 Unit 2 and *por eso* from A2 Unit 5. *Porque* gives the reason ("because"); *por eso* gives the result ("that is why"). They are the simplest tools for explaining nature: why a lake has waves, why an island has a strange shape.

sections.title: Reason or result?
rows: Ometepe tiene forma de ocho porque la forman dos volcanes.
reason: Ometepe is shaped like an eight because two volcanoes form it
El lago es muy grande; por eso a veces tiene olas como el mar.
result: the lake is very big; that is why it sometimes has waves like the sea
La isla es de origen volcánico; por eso su tierra es fértil.
result: the island is volcanic; that is why its soil is fertile
¿Por qué lo llamaron «la Mar Dulce»? Porque parecía un mar.
question and answer: why did they call it "the Sweet Sea"? Because it looked like a sea

items.spanish: Los españoles lo llamaron «la Mar Dulce» porque parecía un mar, pero su agua era dulce.
items.english: The Spaniards called it "the Sweet Sea" because it looked like a sea, but its water was fresh.

items.spanish: El volcán Concepción está activo; por eso se vigila con cuidado.
items.english: The Concepción volcano is active; that is why it is watched carefully.

items.spanish: En el lago hay tiburones porque el río San Juan lo une con el mar Caribe.
items.english: There are sharks in the lake because the San Juan river joins it to the Caribbean Sea.

items.spanish: Hay muchas islas pequeñas cerca de Granada porque un volcán cambió el paisaje hace miles de años.
items.english: There are many small islands near Granada because a volcano changed the landscape thousands of years ago.

sections.content: *Porque* (one word, no accent) gives a reason; *por qué* (two words, with an accent) asks "why?". *Por eso* starts a new clause, after a semicolon or a full stop: not *…; porque a veces tiene olas*, when you mean "that is why".
